subject: Generalize the taskq decode to every agent: move it to the engine seam and wire Codex
description:
v1.116.0-v1.117.0 taught the Claude adapter to turn `taskq` CLI traffic into `TaskOp`s, so
sessions that manage work through the shared queue stop rendering an empty task panel. The
DECODE is agent-neutral - it depends only on taskq's own contract (a `##taskq/v1 {json}` line
last on stdout, plus the `--subject`/`--description`/`--active-form` flags on the command) -
but it lives PRIVATE inside claude-replay-agents/src/agents/claude/model.rs. So:

  - Claude Code: works.
  - QoderWork: works already, for free, because QoderWorkAdapter delegates `decode_line`
    straight to the Claude family.
  - Codex: does NOT work. Never wired.
  - A third-party adapter built against claude-replay-engine: cannot reach it at all. That is
    the real generality gap - agent-neutral code sitting inside one agent's family.

WORK:

1. Move `shell_words`, `TaskqCall`, `taskq_calls`, `taskq_create_ops` and `taskq_ops` (plus
   their unit tests) out of agents/claude/model.rs into a new
   claude-replay-engine/src/engine/taskq.rs, and export them on
   claude-replay-engine/src/engine/seam.rs. The `agents_import_only_the_seam` audit test will
   fail loudly if the Claude family still reaches in by any other path.

2. Change `taskq_create_ops` to take `&str` (the command line) rather than `&Value` - today it
   hardcodes Claude's `input.command` key. `taskq_calls` underneath is already neutral.

3. Wire Codex. Its shell tool names are `exec` | `exec_command` | `shell` | `shell_command` |
   `bash`, and its command arrives either as `input.cmd` (a string) or as an argv array like
   ["/bin/zsh","-lc","taskq create ..."]. `command_execution_text()` in
   claude-replay-agents/src/agents/codex/model.rs ALREADY unwraps both forms including the
   `-lc` case, so use it. Pair creates to their ids using Codex's `call_id`.

   IMPORTANT: Codex has TWO decode paths, and `codex_task_op` is pushed at BOTH (around lines
   216 and 1143 of that file). Hook both, or the equivalence gate will catch it.

4. Add a Codex wiring test; there are `exec_command` fixtures around line 2835 to crib from.

VERSIONS: bump FOLD_VERSION in claude-replay-engine/src/engine/meta_stream.rs - the fold now
emits ops it did not before for Codex sessions, and durable streams must be invalidated. Do
NOT bump RECORD_SCHEMA by reflex: v1.116.1 (commit 077f793) changed which task ops the fold
emits and bumped FOLD_VERSION alone, and the served view picked it up correctly.

GATES: the usual five (fmt, clippy --all-targets, test, scripts/gate/gate.sh printing
BYTE-IDENTICAL: PASS, rustdoc with --deny warnings). Plus, because this is an adapter
event-mapping change, docs/adapter-rendering-validation.md applies: render a minimal
Claude-shaped reference and a Codex transcript through the same binary and options, and
compare their semantics under default and --full.

The byte gate should pass with NO re-baseline - for Claude this is a pure code move. Any diff
is semantic drift; inspect it rather than re-baselining past it.

KNOWN LIMITS, deliberately out of scope: `log` records map to nothing (they change no rendered
field); `archive`/`delete`/`renumber` are unmapped (they mean "leave the list", which an
append-only fold cannot express - the same reason `Snapshot` exists for TodoWrite); the
`--user` queue is not distinguished from the repo queue in the panel; and a taskq record is
lost if its Bash result's stdout exceeds ELIDE_STRING_BYTES (64 KB), because elision keeps only
POSTFIX_KEEP (64 bytes) of the tail and a record line is longer than that.
activeForm: Generalizing the taskq decode to every agent
